exampleAnswers.title: Computing the One-Sided Limits of a Piecewise Function when the Limits Coincide

question.text: Find the left- and right-sided limits at $x=0$ of the piecewise function $f(x)$ defined by \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} -x +1 &\textrm{ for }\quad x \leq 0 \\ \sin x +1 &\textrm{ for }\quad x > 0. \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
Approaching from the left, we have $x< 0,$ so we use the expression $f(x) = -x+1.$ We get

\begin{align} \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 0^{-}}f(x)&=\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 0^{-}} \left(-x+1 \right)\\[3pt] &=-(0)+1\\[3pt] &=1. \end{align}

Now, approaching from the right, we have $x \gt 0,$ so we use the expression $f(x) = \sin x +1.$ We get

\begin{align} \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 0^{+}}f(x)&=\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 0^{+}} \sin x+1\\[3pt] &=\sin 0 +1\\[3pt] &=0+1\\[3pt] &=1. \end{align}

Therefore, we conclude that \[ \lim_\limits{x \to 0^{-}} f(x)=\lim_\limits{x \to 0^{+}} f(x)=1. \]

question.text: Find the right-sided limit at $x=-4$ of the piecewise function $f(x)$ defined by \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} -16 \quad &\textrm{ for }\quad x\leq -4 \\ x^2 \quad &\textrm{ for }\quad x > -4. \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
Approaching from the right, we have $x\gt-4,$ so we use the expression $f(x) = x^2.$ We get

\begin{align*} \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \left(-4\right)^+}f(x)&=\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \left(-4\right)^+} x^2\\[3pt] &=\left(-4\right)^2\\[3pt] &=16. \end{align*}

example.title: Computing the One-Sided Limits of a Piecewise Function when the Limits Coincide

question.text:
Find the limit at $x = 1$ of the piecewise function $f(x)$ defined by
\[
f(x) = 
\begin{cases}
2x - 1 \quad    &\textrm{ for }\quad x < 1 \\[5pt]
2 \quad    &\textrm{ for }\quad x = 1 \\[5pt]
2 - x^{2} \quad   & \textrm{ for }\quad x \gt 1.
\end{cases}
\]
question.explanation:
Approaching from the left, we have $x< 1,$ so we use the expression $f(x) = 2x - 1.$ We get \begin{align} \lim_\limits{x \rightarrow 1^{-}} f(x) & = \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 1^{-}} (2x - 1) \\[5pt] & = 2(1) - 1 \\[5pt] &= 1. \end{align}

Approaching from the right, we have $x \gt 1,$ so we use the expression $f(x) = 2 - x^{2}.$ We get \begin{align} \lim_\limits{x \rightarrow 1^{+}} f(x) & = \lim_\limits{x \rightarrow 1^{+}} \left(2 - x^{2}\right) \\[5pt] & = 2 - 1^{2} \\[5pt] &= 1. \end{align}

Since the left- and right-sided limits are equal to $1,$ we conclude that \[ \lim_\limits{x \to 1} f(x) = \bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{1}. \]

example.title: Computing the One-Sided Limits of a Piecewise Function when the Limits Coincide

question.text: Find the limit at $x=0$ of the piecewise function $f(x)$ defined by \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} e^x +1 &\textrm{ for }\quad x< 0 \\ 1 &\textrm{ for }\quad x= 0 \\ e^{-x} +1 &\textrm{ for }\quad x > 0. \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
Approaching from the left, we have $x< 0,$ so we use the expression $f(x) = e^x+1.$ We get

\begin{align} \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 0^{-}}f(x)&=\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 0^{-}} \left(e^x+1\right)\\[3pt] &=e^{0}+1\\[3pt] &=1+1\\[3pt] &=2. \end{align}

Approaching from the right, we have $x\gt 0,$ so we use the expression $f(x) = e^{-x} +1.$ We get

\begin{align} \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 0^{+}}f(x)&=\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 0^{+}} \left(e^{-x}+1\right) \\[3pt] &=e^{-0}+1 \\[3pt] &=1+1\\[3pt] &=2. \end{align}

Since the left- and right-sided limits are equal to $2,$ we conclude that \[ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 0}f(x)=2. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Computing the One-Sided Limits of a Piecewise Function when the Limits Do Not Coincide

question.text:
Find the left-sided and the right-sided limits at $x= 4$ for the function

\[ g(x)=\begin{cases} x + 2 &\textrm{ for }\quad x < 4\\[5pt] e^{x-4} +1 &\textrm{ for }\quad x \geq 4. \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
Approaching from the left, we have $x < 4,$ so we use the expression $g(x) = x - 2.$ We get

\begin{align} \lim_\limits{x \to 4^{-}} g(x)&=\lim_\limits{x \to 2^{-}} \left( x + 2\right) \\[5pt] &= 4 + 2 \\[5pt] &= 6. \end{align}

Approaching from the right, we have $x \gt 4,$ so we use the expression $g(x) =e^{x-4} +1.$ We get

\begin{align} \lim_\limits{x \to 4^{+}} g(x)&=\lim_\limits{x \to 4^{+}}(\, e^{x-4} +1\, )\\[5pt] &= e^{4-4} +1 \\[5pt] &=e^{0} +1 \\[5pt] &= 2. \end{align}

Therefore,
\[ \lim_\limits{x \to 4^{-}} g(x)= \bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{6}, \quad \lim_\limits{x \to 4^{+}} g(x) = \bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{2}. \]

example.title: Computing the One-Sided Limits of a Piecewise Function when the Limits Do Not Coincide

question.text:
Find the right-sided limit at $x=32$ for the function
\[
f(x) = 
\begin{cases}
2x \quad &\textrm{ for }\quad x\leq 32\\[5pt]
\sqrt[5]{x}  \quad   &\textrm{ for }\quad x > 32.
\end{cases}
\]
question.explanation:
Approaching from the right, we have $x > 32,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=\sqrt[5]{x}.$ We get

\begin{align*} \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 32^+}f(x)&=\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 32^+} \sqrt[5]{x} \\[3pt] &=\sqrt[5]{32} \\[3pt] &=\bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{2}. \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Computing Limits of Piecewise Functions with a Gap in the Domain

question.text: Find $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,0^{+}}f(x)$ and $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,0^{-}}f(x)$ for the function given by \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} e^x + 1 &\textrm{ for }\quad x\leq 0 \\[5pt] \sqrt{x}+2 &\textrm{ for }\quad x \geq 1 \\[5pt] \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
Approaching $x=0$ from the left, we have $x \lt 0,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=e^x + 1.$ We get \begin{align} \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 0^{-}}f(x)&=\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 0^{-}} \left(e^x+1\right) \\ &=e^0+1\\ &=1+1\\ &=2. \end{align}

The right-sided limit $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 0^+}f(x)$ does not exist since $f(x)$ is not defined on the interval $x\in(0,1).$

Consequently,

\[ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 0^+}f(x) = \text{DNE}. \]

Therefore, \[ \lim_\limits{x \to 0^{-}} f(x)=2, \quad \lim_\limits{x \to 0^{+}} f(x)=\textrm{DNE}. \]

example.title: Computing Limits of Piecewise Functions with a Gap in the Domain

question.text: Find $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \left(\pi/2\right)}f(x)$ for the function given by \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \sin x \quad &\textrm{ for }\quad -\dfrac{\pi}{2} \leq x \leq \dfrac{\pi}{2} \\ \cos x \quad &\textrm{ for }\quad \pi \leq x \leq 2\pi. \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
To compute $\lim\limits_{x \to \, (\pi/2)} f(x),$ we must compute the left and right-sided limits separately.

However, the right-sided limit $\lim_\limits{x \to \, (\pi/2)^+}f(x)$ does not exist since $f(x)$ is not defined on the interval $x\in\left( \dfrac\pi 2, \pi\right).$

Consequently, the overall limit does not exist either:

\[ \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow (\pi/2)}f(x) = \text{DNE}. \]

example.title: Computing Limits of Piecewise Functions with a Gap in the Domain

question.text:
Find $\lim_\limits{x \to (-2)^{-}}f(x)$ and $\lim_\limits{x \to 4^{+}}f(x)$ for the function given by
\[
f(x) = 
\begin{cases}
(x + 2)^{3} + 7 &\textrm{ for }\quad x \lt -2 \\[5pt]
\sqrt{x - 4} - 1 &\textrm{ for }\quad x \geq 4.
\end{cases}
\]
question.explanation:
Approaching $x = -2$ from the left, we have $x \lt -2,$ so we use the expression $f(x) = (x + 2)^{3} + 7.$ We get \begin{align} \lim_\limits{x \to (-2)^{-}}f(x) & = \lim_\limits{x \to (-2)^{-}} \Big[ (x + 2)^{3} + 7 \Big] \\[3pt] & = (-2 + 2)^{3} + 7 \\[3pt] &= 0^{3} + 7 \\[3pt] & = \bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{7}. \end{align}

On the other hand, approaching $x = 4$ from the right, we have $x \geq 4,$ so we use the expression $f(x) = \sqrt{x - 4} - 1.$ We get \begin{align} \lim_\limits{x \to 4^{+}}f(x) & = \lim_\limits{x \to 4^{+}} \left(\sqrt{x - 4} - 1\right) \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{4 - 4} - 1 \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{0} - 1 \\[3pt] &= \bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{-1}. \end{align}

exampleAnswers.title: Solving for a Constant Such that the Limit of a Piecewise Function Exists

question.explanation:
In order for $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 2}f(x)$ to exist, the left and right-sided limits must both exist and be equal.

  • Approaching from the left, we have $x < 2,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=c.$ We get \[ \begin{align} \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 2^{-}}f(x)&=\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 2^{-}}c\\[5pt] &=c \,. \end{align} \]

  • Approaching from the right, we have $x>2,$ so we use the expression $f(x)= x^3-3.$ We get \[ \begin{align} \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 2^{+}}f(x)&=\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 2^{+}}x^3-3\\[5pt] &=\left(2\right)^3-3\\[5pt] &=8-3\\[5pt] &=5 \,. \end{align} \]

Finally, since the left and right-sided limits must be equal, we have \[ \begin{align} \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 2^{-}}f(x)&=\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 2^{+}}f(x) \\[5pt] c&=5. \end{align} \]

example.title: Solving for a Constant Such that the Limit of a Piecewise Function Exists

question.text: For the piecewise function \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} 2\tan\left(\dfrac{x\pi}{4}\right)+3x \quad &\textrm{ for }\quad -2 < x\leq 1\\[5pt] 4\cot\left(\dfrac{x\pi}{4}\right)+kx \quad &\textrm{ for }\quad 1 < x < 4 \end{cases} \] it is known that $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 1}f(x)$ exists. What is the value of constant $k?$
question.explanation:
In order for $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 1}f(x)$ to exist, the left and right-sided limits must both exist and be equal.

  • Approaching from the left, we have $x < 1,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=2\tan\left(\dfrac{x\pi}{4}\right)+3x.$ We get \[ \begin{align} \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 1^{-}}f(x)&=\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 1^{-}}\left(2\tan\left(\dfrac{x\pi}{4}\right)+3x\right)\\[5pt] &=2\tan\left(\dfrac{1\cdot \pi}{4}\right)+3(1)\\[5pt] &=2\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)+3\\[5pt] &=2\cdot 1+3\\[5pt] &=5. \end{align} \]

  • Approaching from the right, we have $x>1,$ so we use the expression $f(x)= 4\cot\left(\dfrac{x\pi}{4}\right)+kx.$ We get \[ \begin{align} \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 1^{+}}f(x)&=\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 1^{+}}\left(4\cot\left(\dfrac{x\pi}{4}\right)+kx\right)\\[5pt] &=4\cot\left(\dfrac{1\cdot \pi}{4}\right)+k(1)\\[5pt] &=4\cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)+k\\[5pt] &=4\cdot 1+k\\[5pt] &=4+k. \end{align} \]

Finally, since the left and right-sided limits must be equal, we have \[ \begin{align} \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 1^{+}}f(x)&=\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 1^{-}}f(x)\\[5pt] 4+k&=5 \\[5pt] k&=1 \,. \end{align} \]
